dependencies.reason: uses its router, error envelope and platform interfaces
uses its credential identity, scope check and organization membership lookup
uses its workspace record, its access decision at private and at read and write levels, and the secret store interface with the encryption it defined

tasks.title: Store entries under the shared rules and serve the secret routes
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the entry validation, entry store and secret routes test files, and confirm they fail
Define the entry table for both kinds at the three scopes, with a migration the second target runs too

Implement the shared rules once: the key shape, the 255-character key limit, case-insensitive matching for lookup and uniqueness, the 262144-byte value limit, the 100-entry cap per scope and case-insensitive ordering of every list
Make a create atomic across its entries, so a duplicate or an over-full scope writes none of them
Serve the four user secret routes, refusing an admin token with 403 because it has no user
Serve the four organization secret routes by slug, for members and admin tokens, refusing an unknown organization and a non-member alike with 404
Serve the four workspace secret routes at private access, so a member of the workspace's organization is refused 404 as a stranger is
Refuse a replace with no value with 400 and an unknown key on replace or delete with 404, changing nothing

tasks.title: Keep secret values out of responses, the store and the logs
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the secret routes' and the secret store's test files, and confirm they fail
Give the secret routes a serialiser that cannot emit a value, rather than one that omits it, so a new route cannot leak one by forgetting
Encrypt every secret value through the secret store before it reaches the relational store, and decrypt only where the service itself uses the value
Confirm by test that a raw dump of the store holds the keys and none of the values
Scrub secret values from log records on the success, refusal and unhandled-failure paths alike

tasks.title: Serve the variable routes at their own access levels
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the variable routes' test files, and confirm they fail
Serve the four variable routes at each of the three scopes over the same entry store, returning the value in every response
Apply the shared key, size, count, duplicate and ordering rules to the variable routes without reimplementing them
Require read access to read a workspace's variables and write access to change them, so a member lists them and is refused 403 forbidden on a write
Confirm that a variable whose key matches a workspace setting changes no setting and no behaviour those settings govern

tasks.title: Resolve a workspace's variables from the owner outwards
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the resolved view's test files, and confirm they fail
Implement the merge: a workspace value overrides an organization value, which overrides a user value, each surviving entry reporting its origin
Take the user tier from the workspace's owner and never from the caller, so every caller with read access gets the same answer
Include the organization tier only when the workspace's owner is a member of the workspace's organization
Return the result sorted by key ignoring case
Serve the route at read access, so a member of the organization receives the owner's answer

tasks.title: Verify storage, resolution and access against a running deployment
steps: Add the three smoke tests and confirm each passes against a running deployment, or skips with a message naming the missing deployment

Trace 04-PATH-1: the create route validates through the shared rules, writes through the secret store's encryption into the relational store, and the list route reads back through the serialiser that cannot emit a value. Confirm no step is served by a stub
Trace 04-PATH-2: the resolved view reads all three tiers from the entry store and the owner from the workspace record, with no tier served from a fixture
Trace 04-PATH-3: the variable list and the variable create reach the access decision of package 03 at read and write level respectively, and the secret list reaches it at private level

For every criterion carrying a contract, confirm a caller in production code consumes the producer's result and not only a test: the shared rules are called by both kinds at all three scopes, the encryption by every secret write, and the access decision by the workspace routes of both kinds
Confirm the creation credentials package 03 writes are readable through this package's store, so the two are one store and not two
Grep src/ and the files every task's touches lists for TODO, FIXME and the project's not-implemented marker, and remove any that remain
Add the secrets and variables conformance cases to the harness from package 01
done_when: `make check` passes with no network access and no deployment configured
afc secrets create, list, update and delete and afc vars create, list, update, delete and resolve behave as docs/prd/cli.md specifies against a running deployment
